The Bunker brothers were born on May 11, 1811 near Bangkok, in the Kingdom of Siam (today's Thailand). The brothers were joined at the sternum by a small piece of cartilage, and though their livers were fused, they were independently complete.

In 1829, Robert Hunter, a Scottish merchant who lived in Bangkok, paid their parents to permit him to exhibit their sons as a curiosity on a world tour. When their contract with Hunter was over, the brothers bought a farm in North Carolina and slaves to do the work they could not do themselves. They married local women on April 13, 1843. Chang wed Adelaide Yates (1823-1917), while Eng married her sister, Sarah Anne (1822-1892). Chang and Adelaide would become the parents of eleven children. Eng and Sarah had ten. After a number of years, the sisters began to dislike each other and separate households were set up and the brothers would move between the two.

In 1870, Chang suffered a stroke, his health declined and he also began drinking heavily (Chang's drinking did not affect Eng as they did not share a circulatory system). Despite his brother's ailing condition, Eng remained in good health. Shortly before his death, Chang was injured after falling from a carriage. He then developed a severe case of bronchitis. On January 17, 1874, Chang died while the brothers were asleep. Eng awoke to find his brother dead and cried, "Then I am going". A doctor was summoned to perform an emergency separation, but he was too late. Eng died approximately three hours later.
